instructions: At least 1 hour before you want them, or up to a week ahead, line an 8 inch square pan with parchment paper, leaving some hanging over two sides.
In a large bowl, stir together the 1 cup peanut butter, 2/3 cup honey, 1 tsp vanilla and 1/2 tsp salt until smooth.
Add the 2 1/2 cups oats, 1/3 cup chocolate chips and 3 tbsp pepitas. It looks too dry at first, so keep stirring until every oat is coated and it holds together.

Transfer it into the pan and spread it out. Lay a second sheet of parchment on top and press down hard with the bottom of a measuring cup, right into the corners. Press firmly, or the bars will crumble when you cut them.
Put the pan in the fridge for at least 1 hour, until the slab feels firm.
Lift it out by the parchment and cut it into 8 bars. Keep them in a sealed container in the fridge for up to a week.
advance_prep_notes: make them at least 1 hour ahead so they can chill before cutting
method_notes: Both versions bind rolled oats with honey and add a little salt and vanilla. Love and Lemons (the lead) makes them with no baking: peanut butter and honey stirred with oats, mini chocolate chips and pepitas, pressed into an 8 inch pan and chilled for an hour. Once Upon a Chef toasts the oats, nuts and coconut, binds them with a boiled honey, brown sugar and butter syrup plus crisp rice cereal and dried fruit, and bakes them at 300°F for a crisp bar. Love and Lemons and Once Upon a Chef both round to 4.8, so the one with more ratings leads. One pan makes 8 bars, which covers two snacks for four.
